summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour delivers a detailed lecture on the proper form of prostration (sujud) in Islamic prayer, drawing from classical Islamic texts. He emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) commanded Muslims to prostrate on seven body parts: the forehead, nose, two hands, two knees, and the tips of two feet. Sh. Ali Mashhour stresses that the nose must touch the ground just as the forehead does, and that many Muslims perform prayer improperly despite years of practice. He uses the analogy of storing valuable diamonds in a safe to illustrate how Muslims should be meticulous about their prayer, checking and rechecking their form just as one would obsess over securing something precious. Sh. Ali Mashhour concludes by noting that only true believers benefit from reminders, citing Quranic verse and Sahih Bukhari to emphasize the importance of continuous learning from those of knowledge both above and beside oneself.
suggested_title: The Seven Points of Prostration: Perfecting Your Prayer Form
